question: What happens if you fall into a black hole?
short_answer: Falling into a stellar-mass black hole causes extreme tidal forces to stretch your body vertically and compress it horizontally—a phenomenon called spaghettification. Near supermassive black holes, you cross the event horizon before tidal forces tear you apart.
full_explanation: Gravity strength drops off with the square of distance. Near a compact black hole, the gravitational pull on your feet is dramatically higher than on your head, pulling your body into a thin strand of particles before reaching the central singularity.
